rule: Do not introduce constructor-parameter coupling between separately-distributed providers (e.g. AWS and CNCF-K8s); adding such a parameter makes one provider require a specific version of the other at runtime
trigger: A trigger or operator __init__ in one provider package gains a parameter whose type or default is imported from a different provider package
rationale: Providers are shipped as independent distributions; users can pin them at different versions. A cross-provider constructor dependency creates a hard version coupling that breaks independently-versioned deployments.

evidence.excerpt: users can deploy AWS and CNCF-K8s individually and cross-version
adds coupling between AWS and CNCF-K8s providers packaged into different distributions

rule: When a trigger instantiates a hook via self.hook(), pass all required domain-specific parameters (e.g. virtual_cluster_id) so that cancel-on-kill and other hook methods have the context they need
trigger: A trigger's hook() call omits a parameter that the hook's action methods (e.g. stop_query, cancel_job_run) require at the AWS API level
rationale: If the hook is built without required identifiers, cancel-on-kill paths call the AWS API with None values and silently fail to cancel the job.

evidence.excerpt: hook() passes only aws_conn_id; cancellation calls virtualClusterId=None and fails

rule: Prefer a custom AWS waiter over a hand-rolled polling loop in async triggers; consult providers/amazon/src/airflow/providers/amazon/aws/waiters/README.md before writing a new trigger
trigger: A new BaseTrigger subclass in the amazon provider implements its own polling loop (e.g. asyncio.sleep + status check) instead of delegating to a custom waiter
rationale: The AWS provider has a dedicated custom-waiter pattern that handles async polling; reinventing it in triggers creates inconsistency and bypasses the shared infrastructure.

evidence.excerpt: perfect case for a custom waiter; see providers/amazon/aws/waiters/README.md

rule: When updating system-test example files from Jinja xcom_pull syntax to task.output syntax, retain the old Jinja form as an inline comment so users still on the older pattern can understand the migration
trigger: A system-test example file replaces `"{{ task_instance.xcom_pull(...) }}"` with `<task>.output` without leaving the old form as a comment
rationale: System-test examples serve as community documentation; the output syntax requires getting used to, so showing both old and new helps users who haven't migrated yet.

evidence.excerpt: show both options for a while; show old syntax as comment next to the new
let users know where it comes from if still using old syntax

rule: Every [START howto_...] / [END howto_...] marker added to a system-test example file must be referenced in the corresponding docs RST file
trigger: A [START howto_<name>] marker is added to a tests/system/ file but no matching :ref:`howto/...<name>` exists in the docs directory
rationale: Unreferenced markers are dead documentation fragments that are never rendered in the Airflow how-to guides, wasting maintenance effort and confusing contributors.

evidence.excerpt: howto_operator_sagemaker_unified_studio_notebook_explicit_params marker not referenced anywhere in the docs

rule: When removing SDK parameters or environment variables from a provider's system test, verify and update the minimum SDK version in the provider's pyproject.toml before removing them
trigger: A system-test file removes SDK-specific env vars or parameters without a corresponding version bump or comment in pyproject.toml
rationale: System tests run against multiple Airflow and provider package versions; removing parameters without pinning the minimum SDK version breaks older combinations.

evidence.excerpt: Did you update the minimum version of that SDK in the pyproject.toml file?

rule: Use @tenacity retry decorators instead of time.sleep() to handle transient waits or race conditions in provider system tests and cleanup functions
trigger: A system-test helper or cleanup function contains time.sleep() to wait for an async resource state or race condition
rationale: time.sleep() adds fixed latency and silently swallows failures; @tenacity retries are idiomatic in the Airflow codebase and make flaky resource-state waits self-documenting and resilient.

evidence.excerpt: inclined to retry in case of failure; using @tenacity is easy and clean, many examples in codebase

rule: Tests for AWS operator link persistence (e.g. CloudWatch links) must not gate on do_xcom_push; they should supply a context dict with ti directly to decouple UI-link behaviour from XCom return-value behaviour
trigger: A test sets do_xcom_push=True in order to exercise _persist_cloudwatch_link or similar link-persistence methods
rationale: Link persistence is independent of XCom return-value behaviour; coupling them in tests makes the test misleading and will fail if the two concerns are decoupled in production code.

evidence.excerpt: tests should avoid coupling to do_xcom_push; provide context with ti only

rule: Non-user-facing PRs (internal tooling, build configuration, CI changes) must be placed in the hidden section of provider changelog RST files, not in the public Misc section
trigger: A provider changelog.rst adds an internal/non-user-facing PR entry (e.g. pyproject.toml build config, CI tooling) under a visible section like Misc instead of the hidden section
rationale: Providers are released based on user-visible changelog entries; placing internal PRs in visible sections triggers unnecessary provider releases.

evidence.excerpt: not user facing PR; should be moved to the hidden part; some providers won't need to be released

rule: Use autospecced mocks (create_autospec or spec=) for hooks and async context managers in AWS trigger tests to catch API signature drift against the real hook class
trigger: A trigger test creates MagicMock() without spec= for an AWS hook, its async connection method, or its async context manager
rationale: Unspecced mocks silently accept any attribute access; if a production method is renamed or its signature changes, tests still pass, hiding the regression.

evidence.excerpt: autospecced mocks better validate EmrContainerHook API; avoid silent passes if method signatures change

rule: In async trigger tests, consume the async generator using await anext(generator) rather than calling the dunder method generator.__anext__() directly
trigger: A trigger test calls await generator.__anext__() to advance an async generator
rationale: Calling dunder methods directly is non-idiomatic; anext() is the intended public API and makes the test intent clearer for reviewers.

evidence.excerpt: prefer await anext(generator) over calling __anext__() directly

rule: Sensor and trigger docstrings must describe the granularity they wait on accurately; a sensor that waits for a Task Instance must say 'Task Instance', not 'DAG Run'
trigger: A :param or docstring description in a sensor/trigger says 'DAG Run' when the actual wait target is a Task Instance (or vice versa)
rationale: Airflow distinguishes DAG Runs from Task Instances as first-class concepts; mismatched terminology in public-facing docstrings misleads users integrating MWAA or cross-environment sensors.

evidence.excerpt: contains the Task Instance you want to wait for (not DAG Run)
